# Providers

<!-- Generated by scripts/api_docs.py from the code and docs/api/groups.toml. Do not edit. -->

The model APIs: the contract a provider keeps, and the four that ship.

Names: `AnthropicProvider`, `Finish`, `GeminiProvider`, `MockProvider`, `OpenAIProvider`, `Provider`, `ProviderClosed`, `SampleError`, `builtin_providers`, `replay_for`

## AnthropicProvider

```python
class AnthropicProvider
```

Samples the Anthropic Messages API (`/v1/messages`) for the `ModelConfig` the driver
resolved. `base_url` is the API's root, `https://api.anthropic.com` when unset (a proxy
that speaks the same API may be named; give no `/v1`).

One client serves every sample (see `Connection`). `transport` replaces the network (a
test's `httpx.MockTransport`); `environ` is where `api_key_env` is looked up, at sample
time.

`check` requires a key (`api_key_env`) and `max_tokens` (the API requires it; there is no
default), and reads the options in `_OPTIONS`, refusing any other: `thinking` (an object as
the API takes it: `type` a string, `budget_tokens` for `enabled`, `display`; the API judges
the values, and `check` refuses only what needs a beta header this provider cannot send),
`effort` (a string, sent as `output_config.effort`),
`temperature`, `top_p` (numbers), `top_k` (an integer), `prompt_caching` (a boolean,
default true: mark the system text and the last message for caching), and `extra_body` (an
object merged into the request body last; it may not set `model`, `messages`, `system`,
`stream`, `tools`, `max_tokens`, `thinking`, or a key the model's settings set).

### AnthropicProvider.__init__

```python
def __init__(
    self,
    transport: httpx.AsyncBaseTransport | None = None,
    environ: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    timeout: httpx.Timeout | None = None,
) -> None
```

### AnthropicProvider.name

```python
property name: str
```

### AnthropicProvider.check

```python
def check(self, model: ModelConfig) -> list[str]
```

Problems with the model's settings as this provider reads them.

### AnthropicProvider.aclose

```python
async def aclose(self) -> None
```

Close the client and its connections. Later samples fail.

### AnthropicProvider.sample

```python
async def sample(
    self,
    walk: Sequence[Node],
    model: ModelConfig,
    tools: Sequence[Tool],
) -> AsyncGenerator[Part | Finish | Delta, None]
```

Yield deltas as they arrive and each part once complete (before the first delta of
whatever follows it), then the `Finish`. A failure raises `SampleError` (with `status`
and `retry_after` for an HTTP error, and a `status` for an `error` event of a known
type) after yielding every part the stream had finished. Once `stop_reason` has arrived
the reply is done: the stream is still read for the final `usage`, and a reset, an
`error` event, or malformed SSE after it costs only the usage not yet received.

## Finish

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Finish
    stop: Stop
    reason: str | None = None
    meta: str | None = None
```

The end of a reply: the normalised `stop`, and the provider's own finish string
(`None` if it has none to report), and `meta`: what the response carried besides its
parts, as the text of a JSON object (`None` if it carried nothing). Anything else raises
`ValueError` here.

## GeminiProvider

```python
class GeminiProvider
```

Samples Gemini's `streamGenerateContent` (`?alt=sse`) for the `ModelConfig` the driver
resolved.

One client serves every sample (see `Connection`). `transport` replaces the network (a
test's `httpx.MockTransport`); `environ` is where `api_key_env` is looked up, at sample
time.

Settings: `base_url` defaults to the official endpoint; a proxy sets it. A key is required
(`api_key_env` or `api_key`) and goes in the `x-goog-api-key` header. `max_tokens` is
`maxOutputTokens`, which Gemini counts thinking into. Options (`check` refuses any other):
`temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k` (numbers); `thinking`, an object of `include_thoughts` (bool:
ask for thought summaries, which arrive as `Thinking`; without it none are requested),
`budget` (integer, -1 dynamic, 0 off: Gemini 2.5) or `level` (a string: Gemini 3), not both;
`safety_settings`, a list of `{category, threshold}` passed through, one per category; and
`extra_body`, an object merged into the request last, for what the API has that these do
not (it may not set `contents`, `systemInstruction` or `tools`, nor a key the model's
settings set; its `generationConfig` merges into ours).

### GeminiProvider.__init__

```python
def __init__(
    self,
    transport: httpx.AsyncBaseTransport | None = None,
    environ: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    timeout: httpx.Timeout | None = None,
) -> None
```

### GeminiProvider.name

```python
property name: str
```

### GeminiProvider.check

```python
def check(self, model: ModelConfig) -> list[str]
```

Problems with the model's settings: no key named, an unknown or ill-typed option. An
unset `api_key_env` variable is not one: `tau config check` warns of it, sampling fails.

### GeminiProvider.aclose

```python
async def aclose(self) -> None
```

Close the client and its connections. Later samples fail.

### GeminiProvider.sample

```python
async def sample(
    self,
    walk: Sequence[Node],
    model: ModelConfig,
    tools: Sequence[Tool],
) -> AsyncGenerator[Part | Finish | Delta, None]
```

Yield deltas as they arrive and each part once complete (before the first delta of
whatever follows it), then the `Finish`. A failure raises `SampleError` (with `status`
and `retry_after` for an HTTP error or an error event) after yielding every part the
stream had finished or begun; it carries the meta that had arrived. Once `finishReason`
has arrived the reply is done: the stream is still read for `usageMetadata`, and a failure
after it costs only the meta not yet received. A prompt the API blocked (`promptFeedback`
with a `blockReason`) ends as `End`, the reason in `finish_reason` and the block in
`meta`.

## OpenAIProvider

```python
class OpenAIProvider
```

Samples an OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` endpoint for the `ModelConfig` the
driver resolved.

One client serves every sample (see `Connection`). `transport` replaces the network (a
test's `httpx.MockTransport`); `environ` is where `api_key_env` is looked up, at sample
time.

Options (`check` refuses any other): `temperature` and `top_p` (numbers),
`reasoning_effort` (a string), `include_usage` (a boolean, default true: ask the server for
token counts in the stream; some reject it), and `extra_body` (an object merged into the
request body last, for a server's own parameters such as llama.cpp's `cache_prompt`; it may
not set `model`, `messages`, `stream`, or `tools`).


This provider needs a `base_url`, and reads the options in `_OPTIONS`.

### OpenAIProvider.aclose

```python
async def aclose(self) -> None
```

Close the client and its connections. Later samples fail.

### OpenAIProvider.sample

```python
async def sample(
    self,
    walk: Sequence[Node],
    model: ModelConfig,
    tools: Sequence[Tool],
) -> AsyncGenerator[Part | Finish | Delta, None]
```

Yield deltas as they arrive and each part once complete (before the first delta of
whatever follows it), then the `Finish`. A failure raises `SampleError` (with `status`
and `retry_after` for an HTTP error) after yielding every part the stream had finished
or begun; it carries the meta fields that had arrived. Once `finish_reason` has arrived the
reply is done: the stream is
still read for `usage`, but content and tool-call deltas after it are ignored, and an
error chunk, a reset, malformed SSE, or a missing `[DONE]` after it costs only the
meta not yet received, never the reply. A `refusal` delta is text.

## Provider

```python
class Provider(Protocol)
```

One API family, long-lived: the program that builds it closes it (D15). Owes the
driver `model.md` section 10 (the parts of it built so far).

### Provider.name

```python
property name: str
```

What a model's `provider` setting calls it.

### Provider.check

```python
def check(self, model: ModelConfig) -> list[str]
```

Problems with the model's settings as this provider reads them: a missing
`base_url` it needs, one it has no use for, an unknown or ill-typed option, a model
whose `provider` is not its own. Empty if the model is fine. `tau config check`
calls it for every model that names the provider.

### Provider.sample

```python
def sample(
    self,
    walk: Sequence[Node],
    model: ModelConfig,
    tools: Sequence['Tool'],
) -> AsyncGenerator[Part | Finish | Delta, None]
```

`model` is the session's named model, resolved by the driver at this sample. Yield,
interleaved: deltas as text arrives (`TextDelta`, `ThinkingDelta`, `CallNamed` then
`CallArgs`), each whole part as it finishes, then the `Finish`, then end. The driver
saves only the parts and forwards the deltas. A part is yielded before the first delta
of the next part; a delta that breaks this fails the sample. `tools` are the driver's,
offered to the model for this sample only; they are never recorded.

`sample` assumes `check(model)` returned no problems: the driver calls it first, for
every sample, and fails the sample with the problems listed if it returns any, so
`sample` does not re-check. It closes the generator when it stops reading.

Raise `SampleError` to fail; parts yielded before it are kept. Any other `Exception`
(from `check` or from `sample`) fails this sample the same way, with its message as
`Type: message` and `internal: true` in `meta.error`, and its traceback on stderr: a
bug in a provider costs one sample, never the driver. If the sample is cancelled or
fails, the driver saves the text or thinking whose deltas arrived but whose part never
did. A part yielded while deltas are open must be the part
those deltas were building (same kind, same text), and `Finish` may not come with deltas
open.

### Provider.aclose

```python
async def aclose(self) -> None
```

Close what the provider holds open (connections).

## ProviderClosed

```python
class ProviderClosed(SampleError)
```

A sample on a provider whose `aclose()` has been called, or one cut off by it. Not a
transient failure: a retry cannot succeed, so a retrying wrapper passes it on.

## SampleError

```python
class SampleError(Exception)
```

A sample that failed: an HTTP error, a reset connection, a conversion error. `meta` is
what the response had already said about itself (as on `Finish`), kept on the failed reply.
`status` is the HTTP status of an error response (`None` for a failure with none, such as a
refused connection); `retry_after` is the seconds the server asked to wait (`None` if it
did not say). A retrying wrapper provider reads both (D15).

### SampleError.__init__

```python
def __init__(
    self,
    message: str = '',
    meta: str | None = None,
    *,
    status: int | None = None,
    retry_after: float | None = None,
) -> None
```

## builtin_providers

```python
def builtin_providers(environ: Mapping[str, str]) -> dict[str, Provider]
```

The built-in providers by name (`"openai"`, `"anthropic"`, `"gemini"`, `"mock"`), ready
to hand to `Driver` and `check_config`. `environ` is where the hosted providers look up API
keys. The caller closes them (`await p.aclose()`).

## replay_for

```python
def replay_for(part: Part, provider: str) -> dict[str, object] | None
```

The replay data `provider` may send back for `part`, parsed: the JSON object in
`part.replay.data` when the part carries replay tagged with `provider`; `None` for a part
with none, or with another provider's, which the caller treats as unsigned (`model.md`
10.4). The exact text is `part.replay.data`: string values parse back exactly, but numbers
and escapes may not re-serialize to the same bytes. Raises `TypeError` for a non-`Part`.
